question: Does actual global-load-to-shared-store readiness, rather than traffic volume, explain the missing staging time?

immutable_baseline.physical_useful_work_per_warp_stage: 16scalarU16global-load/store pairs, with predicated branches and some batches in compiledSASS

competing_hypotheses.name: load_return_dependency_dominated
competing_hypotheses.mechanism: An STS cannot issue until its source register produced by LDG is ready. Several independent LDGs may overlap; each still consumes request ownership and issue service.
predictions: Dependent pairs have larger normalized cycles/pair than independent batches on identical warm addresses.
Increasing independent window reduces exposed return waits until request/issue/store service saturates.
SASS confirms intended scoreboard write/req chain; measured change persists after matched-loop and scheduling controls.
competing_hypotheses.diagnostic_not_fit: If L is scoped load-to-dependent-store-ready delay and W independent requests, exposed wait can decrease toward L/W plus service limits. This is a mechanism envelope, not a complete timing equation.

competing_hypotheses.name: instruction_or_service_dominated
competing_hypotheses.mechanism: Address/control issue, shared-store service or global request processing dominate after readiness overlap.
predictions: Independent windows give little speedup after matching instruction counts/order and request footprint.
Request/service throughput reaches a plateau despite larger windows.
Any apparent win tracks changed address/control instructions rather than the requested dependency separation.

competing_hypotheses.name: probe_not_transferable
competing_hypotheses.mechanism: Probe changes cache residency, number of requesters, load width, divergence, register pressure or compiler scheduling relative to full GEMM.
predictions: Correctness may pass while SASS/control/traffic differ materially.
Full-stage prediction using probe parameters fails untouchedstage confirmation.
competing_hypotheses.action: Preserve result as scoped probe behavior; do not insert its latency into the GEMM model.
